summary.oneLiner: FY26 marked record profitability with 27% revenue growth and 37.5% EBITDA expansion, proving resilience despite Q4 headwinds from West Asia conflict which deferred high-value MICE bookings. The strategic pivot away from IT-services dependency (now <10% of B2E) and successful upsell of AI-based expense management tools strengthen the long-term structural thesis, even as Q4 PAT fell 46% YoY due to temporary geopolitical shocks.

one-line thesis: FY26 marked record profitability with 27% revenue growth and 37.5% EBITDA expansion, proving resilience despite Q4 headwinds from West Asia conflict which deferred high-value MICE bookings. The strategic pivot away from IT-services dependency (now <10% of B2E) and successful upsell of AI-based expense management tools strengthen the long-term structural thesis, even as Q4 PAT fell 46% YoY due to temporary geopolitical shocks.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,890mn (Q4, -14% YoY), INR 10,065mn (FY26, +27% YoY); EBITDA: INR 126mn (Q4, -46% YoY), INR 917mn adj (FY26, +37.5% YoY); PAT: INR 82mn (Q4, -46% YoY), INR 468mn (FY26, +28% YoY); Order Book: N/A (Service flow); Net Debt: Net Cash INR 2,230mn. One-offs: Q4 impacted by cancellation/deferral of Middle East MICE groups and elevated airfares compressing margins; Share-based payment spike in people cost.
guidance: Medium-term CAGR: 20% Revenue-less-Service-Cost, 30% Adjusted EBITDA; Q1 FY27 run-rates trending ~20% above Q4 FY26; Expect H2 FY27 to be materially stronger than H1 due to pent-up demand release.
order book & pipeline: Corporate pipeline robust: 55 new clients added in Q4 (INR 2,709mn annual billable potential) vs 40 in Q3; Full year 163 new clients (INR 9,568mn); Retention rate ~97%.
segment / subsidiary detail: Air: Passenger vol +9.6% (Q4), +2% (FY26); Margin expanded to ~4% (FY26). Hotels: Room nights +36% (Q4), +16% (FY26); Margin ~9.25%. MICE: Disrupted in Q4 by West Asia conflict; shifting to domestic/SE Asia. B2C: ~30% of gross bookings, profitable (mid-high single digit margin).
growth verticals / optionality: Mid-market corporate segment (new dedicated sales team); AI-driven expense management (Recap) upsell to 1,300+ enterprise base; API-led distribution scaling with affiliates; Domestic tourism infrastructure boom.
margins & cost dynamics: Air margin improved structurally from 2.7% (FY24) to 4% (FY26); Hotel margin 7.7% to 9.25%. Cost pressure: People cost up due to salary inflation and share-based payments in Q4; Discounting ratio optimized to ~48% of gross take (from 61% historically) driven by B2E mix.
capex / expansion: Focus on technology/AI infrastructure (Google Cloud migration, Diya bot, self-booking bots); No heavy physical capex mentioned; Opex investment in mid-market sales team.
capital allocation: Net cash position INR 2,230mn; Strong operating cash flow INR 761mn (FY26) vs INR 73mn (FY25); Holding company (THCL) sold 1.8% stake to fund legal restructuring (NCLT merger of subsidiaries), no further dilution expected.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical conflicts impacting international travel/MICE; Airfare volatility compressing margins; Agentic AI shifting consumer demand channels (mitigated by B2E focus); Regulatory changes in aviation/tourism.
management quality / tone: Resilient and confident; Acknowledges Q4 geopolitical 'blip' as temporary; Emphasizes structural diversification away from IT sector; Highlights strong Q1 recovery signals.
non-obvious takeaways: IT services exposure reduced from 20% (FY24) to <7-10% of total B2E, de-risking the AI-disruption narrative for corporate travel; B2C segment is profitable and cash-generative, not a loss-leader, providing supplier leverage for B2B; MICE international transactions carry 3x-3.5x value vs domestic, explaining disproportionate Q4 revenue impact.

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.
